newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Williams makes offer for Chubb.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Williams makes offer for Chubb.

text.p: British conglomerate Williams Holdings Plc on Friday made a recommended offer worth 1.3 billion pounds ($2.12 billion) for Chubb Security Plc in a deal which would create a world force in security and fire protection.
Williams offered two new Williams shares and 704.12 pence in cash for every three Chubb shares.
The merged group would combine major brand names in the security industry including Yale, Kidd and Chubb and have combined annual sales of some 2.7 billion pounds.

The move is Williams' second attempt to capture Chubb, after it was thwarted in a bid for its former parent Racal Electronics Plc in 1991, a development that sparked the demerger and flotation of Chubb.
Chubb announced on Thursday that it was in talks which may lead to an offer for the group, sending its shares soaring 82 pence or more than 24 percent to a new year's high of 423 pence.

Williams said its offer represented a 37 percent premium over the closing price of 329.5p for Chubb shares on February 11 before takeover speculation sparked a surge in Chubb shares, which is being investigated by the London Stock Exchange.
"Chubb represents an unparalleled opportunity for achieving our ambition to establish Williams as a world leader in fire protection and security," said Williams chairman Nigel Rudd in a statement.
"The complementary nature of both groups' products and markets provides an ideal blend for the profitable development of the Yale, Kidd and Chubb brands throughout the world."
There was speculation that Williams' offer may require a referral to Britain's monopoly authorities as Williams and Chubb are the biggest suppliers of locks and fire extinguishers in Britain.
However, Williams said it did not anticipate a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission and was confident of obtaining the necessary regulatory clearance.

Williams saw benefits for the merged group in purchasing, distribution and consolidating manufacturing locations amd forecast that by the end of Deember 1998, it would realise cost savings amounting to 40 million pounds on an annualised basis although it would cost some 30 million pounds to achieve these.
The two firms have complementary businesses across Europe, the Americas and Asia Pacific.

Williams said its Yale and Kidde businesses are particularly strong in the Americas and continental Europe and have a growing presence in the Far East, whereas Chubb has limited business in the Americas, considerable strength in Britain and a large presence in Asia-Pacific.
Williams said the acquisition would result in modest dilution in earnings per share (EPS) for the first 12 months before reorganisation costs but expected EPS to be enhanced in the next 12 months.

The conglomerate issued an earnings estimate along with its offer terms, forecasting an 11 percent rise in pre-tax pre-exceptional profits for 1996 to 243 million pounds ($396.5 million) and an exceptional profit of 97 million pounds, up from 9.0 million previously.
It expects a final dividend of 9.25p net, making 15.05p for the full year. ($1=.6128 Pound)
